**Shakespeare plays that mention a pear (directly or allusively)**  

| Play | Pear reference | Source |
|------|----------------|--------|
| *All’s Well That Ends Well* | In Act I, Scene 1 the character Parolles blames the deceased **“withered pear”** for his “delicacy in women” – a concrete mention of a fruit. | https://shakespeare.mit.edu/allswell/full.html (lines 161‑168) |
| *Romeo & Juliet* | In Act II, Scene 1, Mercutio’s one‑liner “**an open‑et‑caetera, thou a poperin pear**” is an allusion to a pear (specifically a pear from Poperinge). | https://shakespeare.mit.edu/romeo_juliet/full.html (lines 2‑6) |

These two works are the only Shakespearean plays that contain any explicit or spoken allusion to pears noted in modern editions. No other five‑act play of his canon contains a reference to a pear.
